name: MindStudio
summary: Visual builder for AI agents and workflows across 200+ models, with model usage passed through at provider cost and no markup.
best_for: operators and teams that want to build and deploy real AI agents and workflows visually, across many models, without engineering time
skip_if: you need one simple chatbot (simpler tools exist) or deeply custom logic that ends up easier in actual code
honest_knock: The no-markup model pass-through is genuinely fair — but it also means your real cost is subscription PLUS model spend, and an agent that loops or processes big documents burns provider credits invisibly until you set limits. The honest build discipline: start every agent with usage caps, and treat 'no-code' as no-code for the plumbing — the logic design and prompt quality are still entirely on you.

pricing.notes:
(prices re-verified 2026-09-18 and again 2026-10-05 on mindstudio.ai/pricing) The subscription is a floor, not the bill: every tier reads “+ usage”, so model calls are charged on top. Free is $0/month plus usage and caps you at one agent and 1,000 runs a month. Individual is $20/month plus usage, or $16/month plus usage billed yearly, a stated 20% saving, and lifts both caps to unlimited agents and unlimited runs. Business is quote-based. Because the metered part is uncapped by the plan, the tier you pick says little about what you will actually pay — the run volume does.

The metered half is more governable than that makes it sound, and the page is specific about it. A run is one execution of an agent, triggered manually or automatically. MindStudio states it does not mark up model cost — its FAQ says you pay exactly the same price as bringing your own API keys from the providers — and that you can set per-agent and total spend limits and track run cost per agent. All tiers reach 200+ models through its Service Router without API keys of your own, with bring-your-own keys as an option, and hitting a run limit triggers a notification with the choice of upgrading or buying additional runs rather than a hard stop mid-month.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 on the Free plan, with no card, no top-up and nothing published: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We had MindStudio's built-in Architect build an agent that pulls record IDs and dates out of four made-up records (one without a date) and tried to run it. The run failed for lack of credit, so the extraction itself was not tested.
findings: The Free plan in the app lists 'One Agent' and '1,000 runs / month', but model usage is paid from a separate prepaid balance that starts at $0.00 on a new workspace (shown in red, 'Click to top up'). Topping up opens a card form with $10, $25, $100 and $500; we did not fill it in.

Our first run of our own agent, in the debugger, stopped while waiting for the model with 'You are out of usage credits' and 'Run Failed: insufficient_credits/balance'. There was no output, so we cannot say how well it extracts dates or whether it marks the record without a date as unknown.

'Generate Agent' started the built-in MindStudio Architect, which first asked three clarifying questions (date format, output format, several dates per record), then showed a readable plan with the rule to never infer, guess or fabricate dates, and built the agent in about one and a half minutes after 'Build'. The Architect's own debug log listed billing events of about $0.88 over ten steps, while our balance stayed at $0.00: MindStudio paid for that work, not us.

The debugger logs every step with timings, the resolved variables, the full prompt sent and the model used (Claude 5.5 Sonnet at 0.5°); the error and its reason appear verbatim. The Architect added a second agent next to the empty first one, although Free names 'One Agent'; both were drafts.

Onboarding offered two ways to connect AI models: the recommended Service Router ('Charged only when agents run', at provider rates without markup) or your own API keys. We chose the Service Router and did not try our own keys.

We found no export or download option for an agent in the editor. The debugger shows 'Open Script' for the workflow and the Architect run has 'Copy for LLM', which copies the conversation; we did not test these further.
not_tested: A successful agent run and the quality of the extraction (no credit)
Your own API keys as a way to run without credit
Publishing, the one-agent limit and how runs are counted
Exporting an agent, its prompts or logs
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

claim_checks.observed: The Free plan page in the app shows '1,000 runs / month', but the workspace credit balance starts at $0.00 and our first run of our own agent failed with 'You are out of usage credits' (insufficient_credits/balance).
claim_checks.comparability: The claim counts runs; we measured whether a run can start without paying for model usage. Different quantity.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: On Free you still need to top up credit (or bring your own API keys, not tested) before an agent that calls a model can run.
